title: Is Your Supervisor Giving Enough Feedback? What to…
summary: Practical steps for IB students who need more EE supervisor feedback during the September-November fall term, including when to escalate concerns.
body_markdown:
### Is Your Supervisor Giving Enough Feedback? What to Do


If your **supervisor is not giving enough feedback** , do not wait silently until the Extended Essay deadline approaches. Request a short meeting, provide focused questions, confirm the next action in writing, and involve your EE coordinator if repeated, reasonable requests receive no response.


Limited feedback does not always mean poor supervision. The EE is independent research, so supervisors should guide decisions without rewriting, proofreading, or constructing arguments for students. This distinction matters during the **IB EE fall term** , when many schools schedule reflections, draft reviews, and final revisions.


### Decide whether the feedback is actually insufficient


The IB requires **three formal reflection sessions** , including a final viva voce. Supervisors provide advice during the research and writing process, but the essay must remain the student's own work. The[IB overview of the Extended Essay](https://ibo.org/programmes/diploma-programme/curriculum/dp-core/extended-essay/what-is-the-extended-essay/) confirms these requirements.


A supervisor might ask, “How does this evidence answer your research question?” rather than telling you what to write. That is appropriate guidance. Persistent non-response, missed required meetings, or refusal to discuss major concerns about scope, method, and progress may indicate a genuine problem.


Situation Usually acceptable Possible concern


Draft comments General comments and open questions No response by the agreed date


Argument Questions logic, evidence, or focus Refuses to discuss whether the project is viable


Meetings Limited but purposeful contact Repeated cancellations without replacement dates


Editing Does not rewrite or proofread Provides no guidance because editing is prohibited


Reflections Conducts the required sessions A mandatory session is not scheduled or recorded


A supervisor can comment on **one completed EE draft** , but should not repeatedly edit successive full drafts. RevisionDojo's explanation of the[EE one-draft rule](https://www.revisiondojo.com/blog/ee-how-many-drafts-can-a-supervisor-read) shows why that formal draft should be as complete as possible.


### Check the rules and deadlines applying to you


September-November is not a universal IB deadline period. Schools establish internal deadlines, often well before IB submission, so your coordinator's calendar controls school meetings and submissions.


You must also identify your assessment session. The revised EE framework applies from **first assessment in May 2027** , according to the[IB Extended Essay curriculum update](https://ibo.org/university-admission/latest-curriculum-updates/dp-extended-essay-updates/) . Under that framework, students complete three mandatory formal reflection sessions and a **500-word reflective statement** on the Reflection and Progress Form, as explained in the official[Extended Essay subject brief](https://www.ibo.org/globalassets/new-structure/university-admission/pdfs/ee_subjectbrief_en.pdf) .


Ask your coordinator, “Which assessment session and EE guide apply to my submission?” Do not combine criteria, forms, or online advice intended for different cohorts.


### Ask for feedback your supervisor can provide


“Can you check my EE?” is vague and can sound like a request for editing. Instead, send a compact feedback package containing:


- Your exact research question
- A current outline or completed draft, depending on the agreed stage
- The relevant school deadline
- A short progress summary
- **3-5 specific questions**


Appropriate questions include:


- Does my method fit the registered subject?
- Which section is least connected to the research question?
- Where does the argument become descriptive rather than analytical?
- Have I overlooked a major category of evidence or perspective?
- Is the scope manageable within the word limit and available time?


These questions preserve your authorship because they ask the supervisor to identify problems, not provide replacement content. Before submitting the formal draft, use the[RevisionDojo guide to improving an EE draft](https://www.revisiondojo.com/blog/how-to-improve-your-ib-extended-essay-draft-expert-feedback-guide) to check that your argument, evidence, conclusion, and citations are present.


### Send a clear written request


A concise message creates a record and makes it easier for a busy teacher to respond.


> Subject: EE feedback meeting before \[date\]
>
>
> Dear \[Supervisor's name\],
>
>
> I am preparing for my \[reflection/draft deadline\] on \[date\]. Could we have a 20-minute meeting to discuss whether my research question, method, and argument remain viable? I have attached my current \[outline/draft\] and four specific questions. I am available on \[option one\] or \[option two\].
>
>
> Thank you,
>
>
> \[Name\]


If there is no answer after several school days, send one polite follow-up. If a required deadline is close, contact the coordinator sooner rather than waiting through an arbitrary response period.


### Follow a September-November recovery plan


### September: diagnose the project


Confirm your assessment session, internal deadlines, research question, and next reflection. Prepare an argument-led outline and identify missing evidence. The[RevisionDojo EE research question guide](https://www.revisiondojo.com/blog/how-to-craft-the-perfect-ib-extended-essay-research-question-8-proven-tips) can help you test focus, feasibility, and subject alignment.


### October: secure the main feedback point


Submit the agreed material on time and request a meeting using focused questions. If this is the completed-draft review, submit a genuinely complete essay rather than disconnected sections. Convert feedback into actions such as “evaluate the limitations of source group B” instead of expecting sentence-level corrections.


### November: revise and resolve barriers


Prioritize the research question, method, structure, evidence, and analysis before polishing grammar. If required supervision is still not happening, contact the EE coordinator before the internal deadline. Bring messages, dates, submitted work, and a concise explanation of the missing support.


### Know when to escalate


Escalation is appropriate when a lack of response threatens a required reflection, authentication, ethical approval, safe experimentation, or an internal deadline. Its purpose is to protect the formal process, not punish the supervisor.


Use this sequence unless school policy states otherwise:


1. Send a specific request to the supervisor.
2. Follow up once after a reasonable interval.
3. Contact the **EE coordinator** with a factual timeline.
4. If necessary, involve the DP coordinator or designated school leader.


For example: “I sent my outline on 18 September and requested meetings on 23 September and 1 October. My interim reflection is due on 15 October, but I do not have a meeting date. Could you help arrange the required checkpoint?” Specific evidence is more useful than accusing the supervisor of being uninterested.


### Keep working without replacing your supervisor


Maintain a dated **Researcher's Reflection Space** recording changes to your question, source evaluations, methodological decisions, setbacks, and next steps. The RRS cannot replace a mandatory meeting, but it provides concrete material for later discussion. RevisionDojo's[RRS guide](https://www.revisiondojo.com/blog/ee-rrs-researchers-reflection-space) explains how to record decisions rather than simply keeping a diary.


An[EE feedback tool](https://www.revisiondojo.com/blog/ib-ee-feedback-tool-improve-your-extended-essay-score) or Jojo AI can help identify possible weaknesses. You must evaluate each suggestion, write revisions yourself, and follow your school's academic integrity and AI-use policies. External support cannot replace supervisor contact or compromise the essay's authenticity.


### Common mistakes to avoid


- **Waiting for permission to continue:** Keep researching, outlining, citing, and drafting.
- **Requesting proofreading:** Your supervisor is not your copy editor.
- **Submitting fragments as the full draft:** Use the formal review opportunity for a complete argument.
- **Changing the question impulsively:** Major changes can affect subject fit, method, and existing evidence.
- **Ignoring internal deadlines:** School deadlines apply even though they vary.
- **Escalating without evidence:** Preserve messages, meeting requests, dates, and submitted versions.


### Conclusion


If your supervisor is not giving enough feedback, clarify the applicable rules, ask focused questions, document communication, continue independent work, and contact the EE coordinator before the delay threatens required reflections or deadlines.


RevisionDojo can support work between meetings without replacing formal supervision. The most relevant options are **EE Support** , **Jojo AI** , and **Coursework Review** for checking alignment, organizing questions, and planning independent revisions.
